editorial.headline: The Public Administration Behind Health Policy
editorial.standfirst: This government health-administration activity is nationally closed to foreign investment and also closed to PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
**This activity belongs to government health administration.** It covers the public work of guiding, advising and making decisions on health services, medicine procurement, public health and disease prevention. Its scope also includes guidance on the provision of clean water. The reference point is a government institution in the health field: an administrative function that directs and considers how health provision is organised.

That public character defines who sits within the activity. It is concerned with government bodies carrying out health-sector administration, rather than a commercial health-service operation. The record lists no business scale as open, reinforcing that this is not framed as an activity available across stated enterprise scales.

At the national level, PMA status is **TERTUTUP**, with a maximum foreign ownership of 0%. There is therefore no foreign equity position available for this activity under the national setting recorded here. This is a closed category, not an activity in which a foreign-owned company can establish a permitted stake.

Bali reaches the same practical result: its status is **TERTUTUP**, and the record marks PMA registration as blocked. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The stated Bali reason is nevertheless precise: it is classified as medium-high or high risk and is not blocked by the province-wide moratorium; verification is required by address. That distinction should not be softened into an opening. The Bali status remains closed, while the cited moratorium—covering low and medium-low risk activities—is not the stated basis for this record's treatment.
